steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Did we really need to be here so early? There's nobody outside the bank right now.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: I have some mint candy, if that'll perk you up.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Appreciate it, but I don't think that's going to do the trick. C'mere, Teacher's Pet. Gimme a good pinch.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Tch...

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Ow!

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Now, let's get to work. Rise and shine, my friends! Hey, I'm talking to you!

steps.name: Blacksteel Squad Member
steps.text: *yaaaawn*... Oh, sorry about that, Franka.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Alright, listen up.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: The bank has a total of four exits. Beanie, take your four people with you and guard the rear door.

steps.name: Blacksteel Squad Member
steps.text: Roger!

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Copperplate, you and Coins will head to the garage door.

steps.name: Blacksteel Squad Member
steps.text: Roger!

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Everyone else, come with the three of us and stay at the front door.

steps.name: Unhappy-looking Resident
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... Excuse me, ma'am. I'd like to ask you something...

steps.name: Unhappy-looking Resident
steps.text: Will you people be out here all day?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Er, yes, we will. But we're simply handling some business and don't intend to interfere your daily affairs.

steps.name: Unhappy-looking Resident
steps.text: Handling business? A few days ago, I signed my pioneering agreement right here. That's the last bit of business I'll be handling.

spans.text: Handling business? A few days ago, I signed my pioneering agreement right here. That's the last bit of business

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Who are you...?

steps.name: Unhappy-looking Resident
steps.text: Hmm... I should at least fill out their customer service review.

steps.name: Unhappy-looking Resident
steps.text: (Checks the thumbs up)

steps.name: Unhappy-looking Resident
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: This bullet... Were you the one who asked Jessica to bring it?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Mm. Found it in an antiques shop in Victoria, a few years back.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: No wonder you searched all over the camp but couldn't find it back then. By the looks of it, seems like one of the officers secretly brought the gun into Victoria.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: And now that the gun's missing, that bullet is the last artifact he left behind.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I warned the fella not to engrave all that flowery nonsense on it... In any case, why didn't you hold onto the bullet yourself?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Because you're the one who should have it, not me.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: What, your ghosts finally catching up to you?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: We were friends once, at least. I can't say I'm happy things ended up like this.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: And do those feelings of guilt and sorrow do you any good?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: What are you after, Woody?

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Call your men back, and stop driving out the residents.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Even if Blacksteel pulls out, the government's just going to hire some other mercenaries. It won't change the outcome.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I heard you initially had the option to turn down the commission. Am I wrong?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Despite its name, at the end of the day Blacksteel Worldwide is still based in Columbia. We don't have the right to refuse a job from the government.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I see, so even you have to tuck your tail between your legs like a normal person from time to time.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: Times have changed. As far as the Columbian government is concerned, soldiers like us mean nothing compared to the geniuses in Trimounts.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Tell me, bossman, what does Blacksteel stand to gain in this contract between the bank and the government?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: This isn't a long-term arrangement, Woody.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: The government has a job for us, so we follow orders and get paid. Beyond that... I don't particularly care, nor am I allowed to care.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I remember back in Laterano. You'd always tell me about all sorts of things, from minor tensions between different groups to massive conflicts between countries... And you'd always put it in the context of how much the people would suffer.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: That was a long time ago. I can hardly remember at this point.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: But I do, clear as day. You told me this on our way from the library to the student dorms: the strong protect themselves, but the truly great protect others.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: So why is it that now, after you've seen these people with your own eyes, you can say you don't care because you're not allowed to?

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: We've both gotten old, Woody. There's a limit to how many things you can care about.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: True enough. But even so, there ain't that many things worth caring about... Everything that's left, that's what's important.

spans.text: True enough. But even so, there ain't that many things
caring about... Everything that's left, that's what's important.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: Maybe I can't protect everyone on the plate anymore, with these rickety old bones. But, the people around me... I'd give my life for them.

steps.name: Woodrow
steps.text: I swear—if any of them get hurt because you got involved, then so help me God I will return this bullet to you. In one piece.

spans.text: I swear—if any of them get hurt because you got involved, then so help me God I
return this bullet to you. In one piece.

steps.name: 'Clip' Cliff
steps.text: ...I sincerely hope it doesn't come to that.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Captain, more and more people are showing up... Do we need to set up a blockade?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: We're not at that point yet. We don't know what the crowd's intentions are, and acting rashly will only make it harder to keep things under control. If dialogue is an option, I'd like to negotiate with the organizer first.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: But... from what I can tell, people have been trickling in since morning. I don't think they're organized.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Nobody's armed, so I'm not too worried about it coming to violence. But, you know, not not worried...

spans.text: Nobody's armed, so I'm not too worried about it coming to violence. But, you know, not

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: After all, the pressure isn't coming from the crowd in front of us, but rather from what's behind us.
The three of them turn their heads and look back at the bank's bright and pristine glass doors and windows.
The sturdiness of the windows blocks out the darkness from the outside, as well as the cold and melting snow.
But no matter how transparent the glass panels are, the warmth and brightness inside will never spill out past the door.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: Captain, take a look at her...

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Helena...

steps.name: Worried Bank Employee
steps.text: Most of them have already signed the pioneering agreement, so what are they all doing, gathering out there?

steps.name: Indifferent Bank Employee
steps.text: What are you worried about? Those aren't toys the Blacksteel people are holding, you know.

steps.name: Worried Bank Employee
steps.text: *sigh* Good grief... And I already turned the TV on to watch the special New Year's interview. I can't imagine what the Governor's going to talk about this year.

steps.name: Indifferent Bank Employee
steps.text: Isn't it the same old song and dance, no matter how they try to spin it?

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Hello, everyone. First, I'd like to wish everyone a happy New Year on behalf of everyone on the broadcasting team.

steps.name: Host
steps.text: During this program, we will be interviewing the Governor and asking him a variety of questions on the issues our citizens are most concerned about. I'm glad you could join us today, Governor.

steps.name: Interview Guest
steps.text: Hello there.

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Just as a routine reminder for our viewers: this program was pre-filmed in September, and the situation may have changed since the time of recording. Please keep this in mind.

steps.name: Interview Guest
steps.text: You only have the scientists perched up in Trimounts to blame for that. Because they still haven't worked out a way to get a Messenger all around Columbia in a single day, hahaha.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Helena, it's so cold out here today. Why are you—

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: I appreciate the thought, but I ain't budging an inch.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I know that you have your issues with the bank... If you have any demands, I might be able to pass them along for you.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: No need to be so uptight, Captain Liskarm.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Most of us here already signed a pioneering contract, and will be leaving with the next convoy. As for what we want...

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: There's nothing left. We're sick and tired of these stupid games, and we're not going to do it anymore.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Then what's the point of you all coming here?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: To take a look.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: At what?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Ever since I was little, I was always told that when you say goodbye to something that's been with you for a long time, you take one good long last look.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: So far... I took a good long look at my diner, at the mining plant, at every last place here on this plate.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: And today, on the first day of the new year, I'm here to take a good long look at the culprit that's making me say goodbye to everything I've ever known.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Ms. Helena, I'm loathe to remind you of this fact, but you voluntarily signed every one of those mortgage agreements yourself.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You're right, I sure did. We walked this path together, but you also pushed us down it.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Nonsense. Take that other gentleman, for example. I seem to recall his business taking a major setback, and no one else would provide a loan. We were gracious enough to lend him forty thousand certs.

steps.name: Furious Resident
steps.text: Right. At first, it was just forty thousand. Not too massive, but not pocket change either. All I wanted was to pay it off as soon as I could.

steps.name: Furious Resident
steps.text: But then you people said I had to properly plan out my investments and liabilities. You said I shouldn't pay everything off in one lump sum along with the interest. You gave me preferential installment rates, and told me to use the leftover money to buy your other financial products...

steps.name: Furious Resident
steps.text: Right. What you lent me was forty thousand, but what you took from me was my store, my house, my car, and even my whole family!

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: We all believed your propaganda and lies at first.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You said you'd make our lives prosperous, and help us achieve a better future. But where do us customers sit at the table of your so-called better future?

steps.name: Furious Resident
steps.text: Right. We were fools blinded by our greed and short-sightedness. We all wanted that little extra something out of life, so we snapped at the bait.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: But, why did we do that? Why was every last person on this plate so desperate, so eager to bite into that life-threatening hook, like a school of hungry fins?

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Is it really our fault? Or has the well been poisoned this whole time–

spans.text: our fault? Or has the well been poisoned this whole time–

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Miss Liskarm, please have these people vacated within ten minutes.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Make it quick.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: (*whispers*) Jessica! Find a way to call up Mr. Cliff! Hurry!

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: On it...

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No good. I can't get through at all.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Keep trying.

steps.name: Jessica
steps.text: No. Sorry, Captain, I need to tell him what's happening here, face-to-face.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: ...Then hurry.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Now then... Helena, Jessica's gone to report the situation to upper management. In just a little while—

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: You ever given any thought to your own future?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I... I've always wanted to start a security company of my own.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Would you take out a loan for it?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Hypothetically, if I had to. Because that's my dream.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: Then you better darn well be careful. That stack of cash only represents the future. It ain't gonna take you there.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: That's the painful lesson the guys you're protecting taught us firsthand.

steps.name: Helena
steps.text: They're liars and thieves. They tamper with the street signs, then turn around and laugh at us for hurtling down dangerous roads in the dark of the night.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I... I understand. I really do.

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Mr. Governor, let's dive straight into the key issues. As we all know, there are still a number of areas in the transitional phase between frontier settlement and fully-developed zone—

steps.name: Interview Guest
steps.text: Most of these settlements in the region are pioneer plates with decades of history and their own core industries, but don't yet meet the standard to be considered nomadic cities. Correct?

steps.name: Host
steps.text: It's just as you say. I've heard that the state government is currently grappling with the question of how to dispose of these plates.

steps.name: Interview Guest
steps.text: Nomadic plates are an important strategic resource, so I cannot agree with your use of the word 'dispose.' Providing assistance to these transitional areas and their residents has become one of the most important items on our desk.

steps.name: Interview Guest
steps.text: For example, additional investment, tax exemptions, school admission discounts, and low-interest loans... All of these policies are designed to benefit people living in just those situations.

steps.name: Worried Bank Employee
steps.text: Manager...

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Fetch the authorization agreement. The one sent by the state government that allows us to mobilize private armed forces in case of emergency.

steps.name: Worried Bank Employee
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Hurry it up. Don't just sit there gawking.

steps.name: Agitated Resident
steps.text: Decades ago, when our forefathers came here, the Columbian customs officials asked about their dreams.

steps.name: Agitated Resident
steps.text: Later, when development on the plate was booming, you encouraged us to stride forward towards a brighter tomorrow. Saying that all of Columbia wanted to hear our enthusiasm.

steps.name: Agitated Resident
steps.text: But now that we're destitute, sickly, and worthless, you're slamming the door in our faces.

steps.name: Agitated Resident
steps.text: That's not how this works! We'll holler, we'll shout, and we'll roar!

steps.name: Agitated Resident
steps.text: So you'd best prick up your ears and listen!

steps.name: Agitated Resident
steps.text: We cry out for a blizzard, and a mighty storm comes♪

steps.name: Agitated Resident
steps.text: Pushed out in the wilds, with hardly a crumb♪

steps.name: Agitated Resident
steps.text: Far, far away, from the lands where we've grown♪

steps.name: Agitated Resident
steps.text: Searching for new lands, new soil to call home♪

steps.name: Host
steps.text: About these low-interest loans...

steps.name: Interview Guest
steps.text: Did I catch you on the back foot? How unusual. Normally, you'd be bombarding me with questions.

steps.name: Host
steps.text: To be honest, I think this is a rather tough question, and hope that you'll answer it truthfully.

steps.name: Host
steps.text: Some believe that providing a deferment on the interest is simply using tax money to subsidize the local economy. Which is not only a waste of money, but also dampens the enthusiasm of the residents and promotes laziness over self-reliance.

steps.name: Interview Guest
steps.text: Speaking from the state's perspective, we have identified specific plates where something similar can be observed, but we must also extend an appeal to our other citizens. Please show patience and wait for our projects in the transitional zones to fully come to fruition.

steps.name: Interview Guest
steps.text: I implore you to have faith that our local residents aren't lazy, but simply need time to rediscover how to use their legs to walk again.

steps.name: Interview Guest
steps.text: The day they're strong enough to cast aside their crutches, they will repay our Columbian brothers and sisters back in full, with their hearts full of gratitude for your generosity.

steps.name: Worried Bank Employee
steps.text: Found it!

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Go and close the windows. Draw the curtains tight, and stay away from doors and windows.

steps.name: Worried Bank Employee
steps.text: What are they doing outside... Singing?

steps.name: Plate Resident
steps.text: The plow trudges on, the hammer strikes true♪

steps.name: Plate Resident
steps.text: With our own two hands, there's nothing we can't do♪

steps.name: Plate Resident
steps.text: Ever since the day we were born♪

steps.name: Plate Resident
steps.text: A heavy burden we've always worn♪

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Your ten minutes are up. Seeing how they still refuse to vacate the premises, we'll have to resort to more forceful measures.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Sorry, ma'am, but we can't do that.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: ...We shouldn't let these sorts of things get between our partnership.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: If you insist on neglecting your duties, then I can only regretfully inform you that your team is now under my direct command.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Who the hell do you think you are–

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: The agreement to reclaim this plate was jointly signed by the local government, the bank, and Blacksteel. There are clauses within it stating that Blacksteel's personnel must obey our commands and mobilize in case of extraordinary circumstances.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: This is an authorization letter sent at the time of the signing. Please take a look.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: You do not have the authority to override our actions, ma'am.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: No, it says it right here in no uncertain terms. I DO have that authority.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Now, Miss Liskarm. Do it.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Apologies, but I'll have to kindly refuse.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: What you are 'refusing' is not a minor request from a small bank, but a direct order from the government.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Don't forget – Blacksteel is only what it is today because of the trust that Columbia has poured into it.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: But... trust is easily broken. Even a tiny breach is enough to tear down everything that's been built up.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Ha.

steps.name: Bank Manager
steps.text: Do it. Do not make me repeat myself.

steps.name: Plate Resident
steps.text: We're the ones who starve, we're the ones who die♪

steps.name: Plate Resident
steps.text: For a null and empty check, we paid the final price♪

steps.name: Plate Resident
steps.text: We're not in that future, my oh my oh my♪

steps.name: Plate Resident
steps.text: Goodbye, my sweet home, a good long goodbye♪

steps.name: Plate Resident
steps.text: Now far, far away, from the lands where we've grown♪

steps.name: Plate Resident
steps.text: Still searching for new lands, new soil to call home♪

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Ma'am, it makes no difference how many times you say it.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I'm not going to open fire.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Let me say this again – I will not open fire, nor will I allow any of my squad members to do so.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: My job is simply to ensure that nobody breaks into the bank and threatens your precious lives.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: And as far as I can tell, these people pose no threat to you, and merely wish to say goodbye.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: My sincerest condolences if your fragile heart is wounded by this.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: After all... Parting is always such sweet sorrow. Isn't that right?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Listen up, everyone. Nobody is allowed to move without my direct order.

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: Roger...

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: Roger!

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: R-Roger...

steps.name: Communicator
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Now, turn around, ma'am. This is what it truly means to sing. So just sit back and enjoy the show.
